newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-GOLD CUP HERO MISSES IRISH TARGET.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-GOLD CUP HERO MISSES IRISH TARGET.

text.p: Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Imperial Call will not run in the Ericsson Steeplechase at Leopardstown over the weekend.
Trainer Fergie Sutherland said his stable star had not recovered fully from a fall at the final fence when he looked set to win on his seasonal debut at Punchestown earlier this month.
"He suffered some bad bruises at Punchestown. The superficial injuries have cleared up but he is still bruised," Sutherland said.
Sutherland's stable-star, a warm favourite to retain the Gold Cup in 1997, is expected to have his pre-Cheltenham run in the Hennessy Gold Cup at Leopardstown in February.

While Imperial Call is expected to be absent, a cast-list headed by three former Cheltenham Festival winners underlines the importance of the four-day Leopardstown Christmas meeting as a stepping-stone on the road to Cheltenham in March.
Seven Irish-trained horses won at the Cheltenham Festival in 1996.

Thursday, the first day of the Leopardstown meeting, sees Ireland's latest equine star Danoli, winner of a top Cheltenham Novice Hurdle in 1994, run in the grade one Denny Gold Medal Chase over two miles and one furlong (3.4km).
Danoli was a faller at the third last on his previous outing in the Drinmore Chase at Fairyhouse on December 1 but trainer Tom Foley is confident he has his stable-star in the right frame of mind .
"As far as I am concerned the most important thing is that Danoli jumps well. If we get beaten, even beaten a long way, and he jumps well I'll be happy enough," Danoli said.
"We've got plenty of schooling into him since he fell at Fairyhouse and he jumped really well when we took him to Gowran Park on Friday. He's really well in himself."
Danoli will face eight rivals including Arthur Moore-trained Jeffell, unbeaten in his last two outings, and English raider Land Afar.

Friday will see Arthur Moore's 1996 Queen Mother Champion Chase winner Klairon Davis face 11 rivals, including Jim Dreaper-trained Merry Gale in the McCain Handicap Chase over two miles and two furlongs (3.6-km).
The appearance of Doran's Pride in the William Neville Novice Chase over three miles (4.8-km) will ensure a good crowd on Saturday, despite the absence of Imperial Call.
Doran's Pride impressed when beating See More Business to win the Drinmore Chase at Fairyhouse, the same race in which Danoli was a faller.
Another good performance from Doran's Pride on Saturday could see him become a serious challenger to Imperial Call in the 1997 Gold Cup.
